issues.title: Fields use a placeholder instead of a label
issues.description: 1 field on "@std/path - Packages" only have placeholder text ("Search for packages"). It disappears while typing and is not reliably announced by every screen reader. The same problem is also on "@std/path - JSR".
issues.fix:
Keep the placeholder as a hint if you like, but add a real label:
<label for="name">Full name</label>
<input id="name" autocomplete="name">

element.name: Search for packages

issues.title: Search result links have very long, repetitive names
issues.description: Each search result is one link whose name contains the package name, its description, then the runtime compatibility twice ("This package works with Cloudflare Workers, Node.js, Deno, Browsers This package works with Cloudflare Workers This package works with Node.js …") and a bare number ("100") that is never explained. Listening to the results list is slow, and the exact match @std/path only comes after two other packages.
issues.fix: Keep the link name to the package name (@std/path), put the description and compatibility in separate text outside the link, give the compatibility icons one combined label, and label the score (e.g. "JSR score: 100%").

element.name: @std/path Utilities for working with file system paths This package works with Cloudflare Workers, Node.js, Deno, Browsers This package works with Cloudflare Workers This package works with Node.js This package works with Deno This package works with Browsers 100

issues.title: Header search field label is announced twice
issues.description: The search field in the page header is announced as "Search for packages Search for packages": its label is duplicated, probably because both a label and an aria-label or placeholder provide the same text.
issues.fix: Use a single source for the name: either <label for="q">Search for packages</label> or aria-label, not both concatenated through aria-labelledby.

issues.title: Button has no accessible name
issues.description: 10 buttons on "@std/path - JSR" are announced only as "button", with no name. A screen reader user cannot tell what they do.
issues.fix:
Give the button visible text, or an aria-label when it only contains an icon:
<button aria-label="Close"><svg aria-hidden="true">…</svg></button>
